_comment_purpose: Reference opencode.json for SpireBench trial-v0 (A0-zero-shot). Place at the user's opencode config path BEFORE starting a trial run, with the maintainer's normal config backed up. See docs/benchmark/protocol.md §Operator responsibilities.
_comment_what_is_disabled: ALL MCP servers — mempalace, context7, sequential-thinking, vscode-mcp, VibeUE, anything else.
Web fetch tool — not configured here; OpenCode honors the agent contract via tools/permissions.
Sub-agent spawning (task tool) — see permissions block below.
All persistent memory and cross-session state.
_comment_what_is_required: PowerShell shell access (the bridge IPC is PowerShell-driven on Windows).
File read/edit within the repo working directory (so the agent can read SKILL.md, JSON, write its run record).
Whatever model provider the trial is testing — operator sets `model` per run.

permissions._comment: Tighten as needed per run. The intent is: shell + repo file ops only.

agent._comment: Forbid sub-agent spawning explicitly — single context, single run.

mcp._comment: EMPTY for trial-v0. Do NOT add mempalace, context7, sequential-thinking, VibeUE, vscode-mcp, or any other MCP server. The bridge IPC is filesystem-based (state.json / commands.json) and does not require an MCP server.
